notes: Researched landmark heights/styles for Harare CBD. See docs/references/LANDMARKS.md for sources. Colours are hex guesses. Entries with part_of are extra footprints of a landmark (podiums, wings, cores); style_confidence rates facade/colour notes separately from height/match confidence. Styles of the photo-checked entries were corrected from freely licensed photos on 2026-09-27; see docs/references/PHOTOS.md.

landmarks.name: Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe
landmarks.streets: 80 Samora Machel Ave (north side), between First St and Sam Nujoma St

style.notes: Photo-checked (see docs/references/PHOTOS.md): NOT a granite tower: a chamfered-octagon shaft of continuous blue-green/teal reflective curtain glass (#5b808c; lit #6d93a9, shade #39555c) framed by slim light-grey polished-granite piers at every facet edge (#aeb0ac). No setbacks, no taper, no roof mast: the shaft runs straight up to a ~4 m light-grey carved granite frieze band (Great Zimbabwe chevron/zig-zag relief) whose facets flare slightly outward as a cornice; a matching frieze band sits at ~level 6. Below that frieze is a recessed, fully glazed lobby storey between raked granite legs that splay outward to the ground, over a 4-5 level grey granite podium with continuous horizontal ribbon-glass bands (see rbz_podium). A ~40 m galvanised lattice telecom mast stands on the low building just EAST of the tower (not on it) and appears in nearly every skyline photo. Clinton & Evans, 1997.

Photo-checked (see docs/references/PHOTOS.md): 4-5 levels of mid-grey granite cladding (#8f9593, darker than the tower frieze) with continuous horizontal dark-teal ribbon windows (~35% glass); the tower above is carried on raked granite legs with a recessed glass lobby floor between podium and first frieze band.

landmarks.name: Joina City
landmarks.streets: Cnr Jason Moyo Ave & Julius Nyerere Way

style.notes: Photo-checked (see docs/references/PHOTOS.md): Pale grey precast shaft (#b9bab6 lit) with continuous horizontal strip windows on the broad faces (dark blue-grey glass, ~40% glazing) and a narrower punched-window bay with a vertical glass slot on the chamfered side. Crown: the top 3 storeys become a full-width CYLINDRICAL glass drum (blue-grey #5a7189 with light spandrel rings), above it a narrower (~60% dia) ~6 m silver ribbed metal drum, capped by a thin flat circular DISC ~1.4x that drum diameter (flying-saucer ring, #c9cac6) and two antenna masts. Model the ring as a solid disc on a drum, not a ring on four posts. Opened 2010.
Shopping-mall podium ~69x104 m: ground + 4 retail floors, big glazed atrium roof lights, 'JOINA CITY' signage on the corners.

landmarks.name: Karigamombe Centre
landmarks.streets: 53 Samora Machel Ave, cnr Julius Nyerere Way

style.notes: Photo-checked (see docs/references/PHOTOS.md): Probable ID (bearings from five viewpoints all put this tower just WSW of RBZ): slender square tower, blue reflective glass (#5177a4 sunlit, grey-blue #677c8a overcast) in horizontal floor bands on all faces, framed by wide full-height light-grey concrete corner piers (#b8b5b3 in sun; they read dark when backlit) with a small emblem high on one pier. Top: a set-back one-storey glass screen/lantern and a slender white conical needle spire (~8-10 m). Overture num_floors=8 is WRONG (20 floors, 92 m). 1985 Clinton & Evans; NBS head office. Mbuya Nehanda statue + footbridges at this corner.

landmarks.name: Livingstone House
landmarks.streets: 30 Samora Machel Ave (north side), between Leopold Takawira St and Julius Nyerere Way

style.notes: Photo-checked (see docs/references/PHOTOS.md): Probable ID (white tower on the N side of Samora Machel just W of the Julius Nyerere footbridge, behind the green-spired church): white/off-white slab (#dfdfda; reads #acbcc0 in shade) with a punched-window grid, a full-height recessed dark-glass bay (#4a5258) down the middle of the long face, a semicircular rounded end bay with narrow vertical strip windows and a dark-glass curved top floor carrying a sign, and a boxy rooftop lift house with a round porthole window. 1960; was the tallest building in the Federation.
Adjoining lower block/podium of Livingstone House (assumed from adjacency).

landmarks.name: Pearl House (Pearl Assurance House)
landmarks.streets: 61 Samora Machel Ave, cnr First St

style.notes: Photo-checked (see docs/references/PHOTOS.md): Slender 1959 slab clad in golden-ochre/sandstone-coloured panels (#c29a4e lit, #736445 shade) with a regular punched-window grid. Roof: PEARL letters on the parapet and a ~8-10 m white/steel sculpture - a stick figure with splayed legs holding a gold sphere (the pearl) aloft - a skyline marker from Samora Machel Ave. (Photos 1995 and 2014.)

landmarks.name: Monomotapa Hotel
landmarks.streets: 54 Park Lane (Overture: Jomo Kenyatta Lane) / Julius Nyerere Way

style.notes: Photo-checked (see docs/references/PHOTOS.md): Concave crescent slab (~18 storeys) facing Harare Gardens. Sandy-beige/tan precast (#cdbd9c; warm light makes it read golden-brown #9f7644), NOT white: continuous horizontal spandrel bands alternating with continuous ribbon windows (light frames, grey glass) on the curved faces; blank solid end walls in the same tan with a faint square-panel texture. Rooftop sign MONOMOTAPA (was CROWNE PLAZA MONOMOTAPA), antennas. Palms and dense garden trees at the foot. 1974, Roy Densem & Partners.

landmarks.name: Eastgate Centre
landmarks.streets: Cnr Robert Mugabe Rd & Second St (Sam Nujoma St), to Third St

style.notes: 1996, Mick Pearce / Arup, termite-mound-inspired passive cooling. TWO parallel 9-storey precast-concrete slabs (eastgate_block_n, eastgate_block_s: each ~142x14.5 m) either side of this ~131x24 m glass-roofed atrium (this entry = atrium; glass roof at ~22 m on steel lattice beams, suspended steel bridges + glass lifts, skywalk at level 2). Retail on 2 lower floors, offices above; parking for 450 cars.

Photo-checked (see docs/references/PHOTOS.md): Long facades: dense grid of deep grey precast window hoods/"teeth" (#c5bbab lit, #534d47 in their shadows, reads ~#5a5953 from afar) with salmon-brick infill panels (#b5957c); full-height precast X-lattice (diamond-braced) service towers at ~30 m spacing that rise one storey above the roof; thin red tile roof strip; ~24 CYLINDRICAL chimney stacks per block (~2 m dia, 3-4 m tall, pale tan with flared caps and dark rings) evenly along the ridge with small triangular vents between. Street entrance on Robert Mugabe Rd: fan of radiating steel rods over an EASTGATE sign, dark-green steel pavement canopy.

Photo-checked (see docs/references/PHOTOS.md): Long facades: dense grid of deep grey precast window hoods/"teeth" (#c5bbab lit, #534d47 in their shadows, reads ~#5a5953 from afar) with salmon-brick infill panels (#b5957c); full-height precast X-lattice (diamond-braced) service towers at ~30 m spacing that rise one storey above the roof; thin red tile roof strip; ~24 CYLINDRICAL chimney stacks per block (~2 m dia, 3-4 m tall, pale tan with flared caps and dark rings) evenly along the ridge with small triangular vents between. Street entrance on Robert Mugabe Rd: fan of radiating steel rods over an EASTGATE sign, dark-green steel pavement canopy.

landmarks.name: Meikles Hotel (Hyatt Regency Harare The Meikles)
landmarks.streets: Cnr Jason Moyo Ave & Third St, south side of Africa Unity Square

style.notes: Photo-checked (see docs/references/PHOTOS.md): North (square-facing) tower, ~12-13 storeys: off-white precast grid - full-height vertical piers between bays of paired dark grey-blue windows with light spandrels (~45% glazing) - and a top storey of 8 semicircular ARCHES (arched attic/loggia) under a thin flat roof; not balcony bands. Hotel founded 1915, rebuilt 1974-76.

Photo-checked (see docs/references/PHOTOS.md): South block seen from Eastgate/the station: grey unpainted concrete slab (~10 storeys) with horizontal window bands and a blank top band carrying raised letters MEIKLES HOTEL facing south over Eastgate.

landmarks.name: Harare Town House
landmarks.streets: Cnr Julius Nyerere Way & Jason Moyo Ave

style.notes: City Hall (1933, Mediterranean/Italian-Renaissance style, Public Works under Major Roberts). Cream rendered walls, terracotta tile roofs, arched loggia/entrance on Julius Nyerere Way, clock tower (~26 m, assumed) over the entrance. Gardens in front with a floral clock and fountain. Footprint 40x50 m U/courtyard shape.

landmarks.name: Parliament House (old Parliament of Zimbabwe)
landmarks.streets: Cnr Nelson Mandela Ave & Third St, north side of Africa Unity Square

style.notes: Photo-checked (see docs/references/PHOTOS.md): Cream-painted render (#dcd2b8) 2 storeys + parapet with a strong cornice line and a ~1 m grey-painted plinth (#5b6267); white-framed multi-pane sash windows; projecting arched entrance porch with PARLIAMENT OF ZIMBABWE lettering and the coat of arms; red clay-tile pitched roof mostly hidden behind the parapet (white gable visible). Iron palisade fence along Nelson Mandela Ave. 1895-99; used by Parliament until Nov 2023. 2022 photo: cool cream walls (south face is in shade most of the day), pale peach gable ends with white trim above the parapet.
Later 5-floor annex (Overture num_floors 5).

landmarks.name: Cathedral of St Mary and All Saints
landmarks.streets: Cnr Nelson Mandela Ave & Sam Nujoma St, NW corner of Africa Unity Square

style.notes: Photo-checked (see docs/references/PHOTOS.md): Rough-dressed brown-grey granite ashlar (#8f806c), not pale sandstone. Square bell tower (~28 m) with twin louvred lancet openings, a round CLOCK face below them, and a green/grey-green copper pyramidal roof with a cross (#6f7a66); nave roofs grey-green. Herbert Baker, 1913-1961.

landmarks.name: Cathedral of the Sacred Heart
landmarks.streets: Cnr Fourth St & Herbert Chitepo Ave

style.notes: Photo-checked (see docs/references/PHOTOS.md): NOT brick: buff/tan rock-faced coursed stone blocks (#ad9d80 albedo; #8e8173 overcast) with a darker stone plinth (#5a4e42). Gothic Revival west front: two square towers with paired louvred lancets and FLAT crenellated tops with corner pinnacles (no spires, ~26 m), central gable with a cross, rose window, lancet windows with tracery, pointed-arch doorway, statues in niches; granite crucifix memorial on the forecourt. 1925.

landmarks.name: National Gallery of Zimbabwe
landmarks.streets: 20 Julius Nyerere Way, cnr Park Lane

style.notes: Photo-checked (see docs/references/PHOTOS.md): Upper storey clad in large pale stone/concrete panels (#d9d4ca), cantilevered over a recessed glazed ground floor on round pilotis; a huge abstract MOSAIC mural (~20x5 m, primary colours on an ochre ground #c8b068) on the Julius Nyerere Way face; a tall clerestory glass band to one side; reflecting pool and sculptures at the entrance. 1957.

landmarks.streets: Julius Nyerere Way / Inez Terrace (Overture: Mayor Urimbo Terrace), between Nelson Mandela & Jason Moyo

landmarks.name: Munhumutapa Building (Office of the President and Cabinet)
landmarks.streets: Samora Machel Ave / Sam Nujoma St

style.notes: Photo-checked (see docs/references/PHOTOS.md): Long 3-storey colonial government block in pale butter-yellow render (#e2d596 sunlit; reads sage #899e84 in shade) with white-framed sash windows, a heavier ground-floor plinth and red-brown clay-tile HIPPED roofs (#8a5a42). A tall square clock tower (~30 m) with clock faces on each side, an open arched belfry and a small hipped cap rises from the Samora Machel frontage. Office of the President and Cabinet.

landmarks.name: Harare Railway Station (NRZ)

match.name: National Railways Of Zimbabwe, Harare Train Station

landmarks.streets: Kenneth Kaunda Ave, at the south end of Sam Nujoma St

style.notes: Photo-checked (see docs/references/PHOTOS.md): Red-brown FACE BRICK (#8a5c46), not cream render: 2 storeys with cream/white trim bands, window surrounds and cornices (#e6e4d6), arched ground-floor windows, a ground-floor colonnade of BLUE-painted cast columns (#365374) under a balustraded first-floor balcony, red-brown tile hipped roofs, and a red cupola (white columns, red dome) on a brick base. HARARE STATION in black letters on a cream band. Platforms: blue steel canopies on lattice columns, black catenary gantries, red-brick signal cabin.

places.name: Africa Unity Square
places.notes: Ex-Cecil Square (1890 pioneer flag site). ~2.4 ha rectangle (Overture land_use polygon, bounds lon 31.05117-31.05288, lat -17.83018 to -17.82846) bounded by Nelson Mandela Ave (N, Parliament + Anglican cathedral), Jason Moyo Ave (S, Meikles), Sam Nujoma St (W), Third St/Patrice Lumumba St (E). Paths laid out as a Union Jack: two corner-to-corner diagonals + a cross (one path lines up with George Silundika Ave), large central fountain (with smaller fountains), lawns, old jacarandas (purple in Oct-Nov), flower sellers and photographers along the edges.

places.name: Harare Gardens
places.notes: Main city park, ~17 ha: bordered by Herbert Chitepo Ave (N), Julius Nyerere Way / Park Lane (E and S) and Leopold Takawira St (W); the Les Brown pool, Monomotapa Hotel and parking occupy the SW corner. Lawns, flower beds, a pond on the north side, a 1930s bandstand (Sunday jazz), restaurant, playground. National Gallery at the SE corner. Approx corners: NW (-17.8235,31.0440), NE (-17.8218,31.0484), SE (-17.8252,31.0492), S (-17.8262,31.0476), SW (-17.8269,31.0448).

places.name: The Kopje
places.notes: Granite hill where Salisbury/Harare was founded (1890), SW edge of the CBD; national monument (~15 ha). Rises roughly 45-55 m above Robert Mugabe Rd (toposcope quoted at 1,539.8 m ASL; PeakVisor lists 1,496 m). Summit reached by Skipper Hoste Drive, a one-way loop from Robert Mugabe Rd/Kaguvi St. Eternal Flame of Independence (carried here from Rufaro Stadium, 18 Apr 1980) and a (vandalised) toposcope at the top. Wooded (msasa), boulders. Summit location approximate (researched ~-17.841, just south of the map bbox S=-17.840); marker clamped to -17.8398 so it sits on the map edge.

places.name: First Street Mall
places.notes: Pedestrianised First Street (Harare's first pedestrian mall), from about Robert Mugabe Rd/Speke Ave north to Kwame Nkrumah Ave (Overture segment lat -17.8324 to -17.8279); Edgars at the Jason Moyo corner, Galaxy Mall, OK, banks. Paved, benches, vendors, crowds; open to traffic north of Kwame Nkrumah to Samora Machel.

places.name: Mbuya Nehanda Statue
places.notes: Bronze statue of the spirit medium Mbuya Nehanda (unveiled 25 May 2021, David Mutasa): 3 m figure on a 1.5 m pedestal on a corner plaza at the Samora Machel Ave / Julius Nyerere Way intersection, with pedestrian footbridges over the junction. Karigamombe Centre on the SE corner.

places.notes: Main kombi/bus terminus for Ruwa, Marondera, eastern & north-eastern suburbs; ~2.6 ha open lot (Overture polygon) east of Fourth St between Jason Moyo Ave and Robert Mugabe Rd; shelters, touts, vendors.

places.name: National Heroes' Acre
places.notes: Out of map: ~7 km W on the Bulawayo/Norton road ridge. 40 m obelisk tower topped by an Eternal Flame (lit 1982), visible from Harare - use as a distant skyline marker only. Coordinates approximate (+-1 km).
